subject: Using 1-element vector instead of a scalar changes results

messages.author: fb1667ba74f25458
messages.subject: Using 1-element vector instead of a scalar changes results
parts:
Hi all,
I've been struggling for a while with a quite complex model involving numerical integration - a simple model with the integrator worked well, while more complex designs always gave divergent transitions. I was trying to built the model incrementally, but even adding the smallest complexities introduced divergent transitions. Now I am asking for help, because it seems that just using a vector with 1 element instead of a scalar in what is otherwise exactly the same model with exactly the same data causes problems. Honestly, I have ran out of ideas how to solve this.

More details on the model:
This is a model of gene expression where the synthesis of new mRNA is governed by the current level of a regulatory protein. In one model ('training-simplified.stan'), only one regulator is allowed. In the other model ('training.stan') multiple regulators are possible. Nevertheless, I modified the models to accept the exact same data format and only call 'training.stan' with num_regulators = 1, so the models should be exactly equal. I've removed all other differences - if you diff the files, you can see that they only differ in added for loops which go in 1:num_regulators (and num_regulators is 1). 

Still one model produces divergent transitions and the other does not. Also there are noticeably different posterior distributions for some parameters.

Both models, data and code to reproduce are attached (the main code is in 'problem.R')

Note that the data I work with is simulated using the exact model I am trying to fit.

My specs:
Stan 2.14.0
Latest RStan built from source (to avoid bug https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/issues/399)
R 3.3.2
gcc (i686-posix-dwarf, Built by MinGW-W64 project) 4.9.3
Windows 10

Thanks a lot for any hints

Martin

I think there is a lesson somewhere here about stepping far away from your problem before asking for help on a forum :-)

Thanks and sorry for taking your time.

Martin
